subject: Proposal: reshaped commitment, annual true-ups, and holdback option
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: reshaped commitment, annual true-ups, and holdback option

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I’m attaching a compact proposal that aims to: (1) accelerate credits for your expected production increase in H2, (2) smooth commit recognition across three years, and (3) include a small contract holdback to accommodate seasonality risk.

High level summary (details in attached PDF):
- 3-year total commitment: 18M token-units (annualized: 6M/yr)
- Year 1: 45% of total (frontloaded to support migration spike)
- Year 2–3: 27.5% each, with quarterly true-ups to align usage and prevent overrun
- Holdback: 5% of Year 1 invoice held and releasable on 6-month operational milestones (uptime, integration checklist)
- Discount bands scale with committed throughput + adoption milestones (see table, p3)

Requested next steps: please confirm if the holdback approach is acceptable to procurement, and whether the team prefers quarterly or monthly true-ups. I’ll loop Finance and Legal once you confirm the structure and we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0134

Attachments: RDW_Horizon_Proposal_v1.3.pdf (PDF), Horizon_usage_snapshot_Q1-2027.csv (CSV)
From: Maya R. <maya@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Cho <brian.cho@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: reshaped commitment, annual true-ups, and holdback option

Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we take this to procurement: 
1) For the Year 1 frontload, can you convert the 45% into an expected average Q3/Q4 RPS (or GPUs) so our infra team can model it?
2) Can the holdback be milestone-based but capped at $X (we have internal policy that caps holdbacks at 3-7% depending on vendor)?
3) What’s the fallback if we underspend Year 1 by >15% — is there a credit against Year 2?

If it helps, we prefer quarterly true-ups but may ask for monthly reporting for the first 6 months of Year 1.

Best,
Maya
Maya Rao
Head of Platform, Horizon Analytics
maya@horizon-analytics.com

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message attached]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal prep — margin and legal considerations (internal)

Team —

Quick internal note before we respond to Maya:
- Finance comfortable with 45% frontload if holdback is limited to 5% and releasable on operational milestones (we want milestone language that’s objective)
- Discount tiers are OK but Legal wants to avoid complex credit roll-forward clauses; prefer simple true-up credits applied in the next year’s invoices (not retro refunds)
- Suggest we offer a capped underspend protection: "If Year 1 actual usage < committed Year 1 by >15%, client can apply up to 50% of the difference as a credit against Year 2 invoices within the first two quarters." That gives Horizon runway but protects Redwood cash flow.

I’ll draft suggested language for the milestone and underspend sections. Marissa — please review the proposed cap numbers before we send.

—Karthik
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: reshaped commitment, annual true-ups, and holdback option

Maya —

Thanks for the great questions; answers inline below and I’ve attached an updated proposal (v1.3) with the clarified language we discussed: 

1) Frontload sizing: Year 1 frontload corresponds to an estimated 1.8x baseline token throughput compared to your Q1 average — we’ve added an expected GPU-hours estimate (p2) to help infra sizing. If you want exact RPS we can map to your model but the GPU-hours estimate should be usable.
2) Holdback cap: we can convert the holdback into a capped dollar amount at 5% of the Year 1 invoice (we show both % and $ on p4). That should satisfy procurement policy.
3) Underspend: Finance proposed a credit policy: if Year 1 usage is >15% below Year 1 committed amount, Horizon may apply up to 50% of the difference as a credit against Year 2 invoices during the first two quarters of Year 2. This is now explicit in section 5.

We’re happy to do quarterly true-ups and provide monthly reporting for the first 6 months. If that model looks right, the next step would be to sign an amendment with these items and schedule a DocuSign review with procurement.

I’ve attached RDW_Horizon_Proposal_v1.3.pdf with the updated numbers.

Best,
Neha

Attachments: RDW_Horizon_Proposal_v1.3.pdf (PDF)
From: Maya R. <maya@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Cho <brian.cho@horizon-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: reshaped commitment, annual true-ups, and holdback option

Neha / team —

Appreciate the quick edits and the explicit underspend language. Procurement confirms the 5% holdback cap and our Legal team has no material objections to the credit roll-forward (they prefer the Year 2 credit rather than refunds). We’re good to proceed with the amendment and will route the DocuSign to the signatory (our CFO) next week.

Can you please: 
- Send the DocuSign-ready amendment (we’ll need signature tabs for Horizon CFO and Redwood VP Sales)
- Confirm expected billing cadence for Year 1 (we propose monthly invoices with quarterly true-up reconciliation)

I’ll ask Brian to schedule the internal kick-off with infra once we have an executed amendment.

Thanks —
Maya
